cards.text: This one's a song of ascents, sung by a whole crowd of "we." They're looking back at the day the LORD restored the captives of Zion. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I'm ALREADY emotional.

cards.question: I bet it felt too good to be real. When the LORD restored the captives of Zion, what does the song say they were like?
Home again, and the sound changes. Then their mouths were filled with ___.

cards.text: Mouths full of laughter, tongues full of shouts of joy. This isn't polite smiling, friend, this is LOUD happy, the kind that gets people outside talking.

cards.question: People outside really do start talking. It was said among the ___ that the LORD had done great things for them.

cards.text: Even outsiders are saying it: "The LORD has done great things for them." When the folks across the street are talking about your blessings, you KNOW it's real.

cards.question: The nations say, "The LORD has done great things for them." When the singers answer, how do they change that line?

answers.text: They turn it into a question
They say it about the nations

cards.question: True or false: Right after saying the LORD has done great things for us, the singers say they are filled with fear.

cards.text: Then the song turns a corner. Same singers, same LORD, but listen close to the next line.

cards.question: After all that celebrating over what the LORD has done, what do the singers do next?

answers.text: Ask the LORD to restore their captives
Send a message back to the nations
Ask the LORD to judge their enemies

cards.text: And they pray it with a picture: "Restore our captives, O LORD, like streams in the Negev." I can just see the water rushing in.
Then the song walks out into a farm field, where people are sowing seed in tears. Friend, I've cried into a batch of dough before, and the dough did NOT care.

cards.question: Crying while they plant, but that's not the end of it. Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of ___.

cards.text: Then the picture zooms in on one person. He goes out weeping, carrying a trail of seed.

cards.question: The one who went out weeping with seed comes back. What is he carrying now?
True or false: The song says the one who goes out weeping might come back with shouts of joy, if the harvest goes well.

cards.text: Out with tears and a trail of seed, home SURELY, with shouts of joy and arms full of grain. Friend, I went into that drawer a quiet, dusty stamper and came out with a whole BAKERY, so believe me, I get it.
